sovereign_country.strategic_role: 北美成熟市场、联邦与省两级公司实体设立（EPC合规）

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid (bijural): Quebec private and commercial law is civil law (Code civil du Quebec, CQLR c CCQ-1991); federal public, tax, and criminal law is common law; Quebec provincial public law operates within the federal-state framework of the Constitution Act, 1867.
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Canada-United States-Mexico Agreement (CUSMA/USMCA), Chapter 14 (Investment) and Chapter 22 (Digital Trade); Canada-US Income Tax Convention (1980, as amended by Protocols)
Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA) between Canada and the European Union
Comprehensive and Progressive Agreement for Trans-Pacific Partnership (CPTPP)
Canada-China Foreign Investment Promotion and Protection Agreement (FIPA) and analogous FIPAs (e.g., Canada-Hong Kong FIPA, Canada-Azerbaijan FIPA) conferring MFN and FET protections

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act, SC 2000, c 17, as amended (PCMLTFA); Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Regulations, SOR/2002-184; Criminal Code, RSC 1985, c C-46, s 462.31 et seq.; Quebec Business Corporations Act, CQLR c S-31.1 (QBCA); An Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises, CQLR c P-44.1, and its regulation, CQLR c P-44.1, r 1; FINTRAC client identification, record keeping, and reporting obligations; Quebec UBO declaration requirements incorporated into the Registre des entreprises under the legal publicity regime.
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_disclosure_level: Government_Only_Access (UBO particulars are declared to the Registraire des entreprises and are accessible to FINTRAC, Revenu Quebec, the Surete du Quebec, tax authorities, and other authorized investigative bodies; the public enterprise register discloses only limited identification excerpts, not the full beneficial ownership chain)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified true copy of passport or national identity document of each ultimate beneficial owner (UBO), director, and officer
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Passport-issuing authority of the jurisdiction of residence, with attestation by a notary public of competent jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille verifying the notary's seal for foreign-origin documents; Canadian-origin documents require only notarized attestation

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incumbency / Register of Directors and UBOs of any corporate shareholder or member
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent corporate registry, company secretary, or registered agent of the foreign parent entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (for states party to the 1961 Hague Convention) or Consular Legalization via the competent Canadian diplomatic mission (for non-Hague states)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized Power of Attorney appointing the Quebec incorporation agent and registered office representative
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the jurisdiction of execution, countersigned by a Quebec notary where required
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization; Canadian notarial certificates are verified by the designated Canadian authentication authority

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter and proof of residential or business address for each UBO and director (issued within 90 days)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Issuing financial institution or public utility provider
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized certification with sworn English/French translation where the source document is in another language; apostille not typically required for bank-issued correspondence

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified corporate excerpt or certificate of good standing of any foreign corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Companies registry or competent licensing authority of the foreign or extra-provincial jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization; extra-provincial excerpts from the Registraire des entreprises are self-authenticating

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory dual-layer screening for all directors, officers, UBOs at the 25% threshold, and authorized signatories: (1) Canadian domestic layer pursuant to PCMLTFA and FINTRAC guidance, including FATF Recommendation 12 PEP definitions (extended to domestic PEPs), screening against Global Affairs Canada consolidated sanctions lists under the Special Economic Measures Act, SC 1992, c 17, the Justice for Victims of Corrupt Foreign Officials Act (Sergei Magnitsky Law), and the United Nations Act, SC 1991, c 13; (2) International layer: OFAC SDN List and sectoral sanctions (required for USD settlement through Stripe Billing and Authorize.Net), plus EU and UK consolidated lists as second-tier reference; adverse media and negative news checks in English and French; re-screening must occur at onboarding, annually, and upon any trigger event (change of directors, financing rounds, or sanctions-list updates).

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registraire des entreprises du Quebec (REQ) online portal 'Registre des entreprises' — https://www.registraireentreprises.gouv.qc.ca, with optional NUANS name search via Corporations Canada for federal/extra-provincial name protection
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Under the Charter of the French Language (CQLR c C-11) and the QBCA, the corporate name must be in French and must include a permissible French legal designation such as 'Inc.', 'Corp.', 'Ltee', 'Societe par actions', 'Compagnie', or an equivalent recognized abbreviation; trade names in another language may be used commercially only if accompanied by a registered French trade name; foreign alphabet names must be transliterated into Latin script with a certified French transliteration on file.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Tokens implying Crown, government, or public authority connection: 'Gouvernement', 'Ministre', 'Municipal', 'Canada', 'Quebec', 'Royal', 'Crown', 'Police' (require prior ministerial or lieutenant-governor authorization)
Financial services tokens: 'Bank'/'Banque', 'Trust'/'Fiducie', 'Insurance'/'Assurance', 'Securities', 'Broker', 'Deposit' (require OSFI or Autorite des marches financiers pre-authorization)

Regulated profession tokens: 'Lawyer'/'Avocat', 'Notary'/'Notaire', 'Doctor'/'Medecin', 'Engineer'/'Ingenieur', 'Accountant'/'Comptable', 'Broker' (require consent of the applicable professional order)
Educational or philanthrope tokens: 'University'/'Universite', 'College'/'Cegep', 'Foundation'/'Fondation' (require specific legislative authorization)

Tokens that are false, misleading, contrary to public order, or likely to prejudice the rights of third parties per s. 22 QBCA and s. 20 of the Act respecting legal publicity of enterprises, including 'Co-operative'/'Cooperative' without authorization under the Cooperatives Act
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection, the REQ issues a written decision stating the statutory grounds. Within 30 days of notification, the applicant may file a request for review (demande de revision) with the Registraire des entreprises, attaching amended proposed names and legal submissions (ss. 31-33, Act respecting legal publicity of enterprises). If the review is refused, the applicant may appeal to the Court of Quebec (Cour du Quebec) within 30 days of the review decision; alternatively, the applicant may promptly file articles of incorporation under a fresh or numbered name accompanied by a new NUANS search. A previously reserved name may not be transferred, and a fresh reservation fee is payable upon refiling.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Conditionally permissible. The Quebec establishment (etablissement) must be a physical street address in Quebec where statutory records are kept and service of process may be effected. A licensed virtual office with dedicated Quebec address, mail handling, and service-of-process acceptance is generally accepted for a low-risk, non-licensed ISIC 4791 subscription box business, provided it is not a bare mail-drop; payment processors (Stripe Billing, Authorize.Net) and Canadian banks may independently verify the address and may decline onboarding if it appears on known virtual-office or high-risk lists, so a distinct operating or fulfillment address is recommended.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low: estimated <5% annual probability of an unannounced physical inspection at the registered office for a standard non-licensed e-commerce subscription business. However, the Registraire des entreprises and Revenu Quebec conduct postal verification and desk audits at a materially higher rate (10-15%) during the first 24 months following QST/HST registration and financial institution onboarding, particularly where a virtual office address is used.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Name reservation and statutory name research (up to 3 proposed names)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory fee tariff under the Regulation respecting the application of the Act respecting legal publicity of enterprises

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Quebec Business Corporations Act (QBCA) articles of incorporation filing fee
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory filing tariff (approximately CAD 215, converted at market rate)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Enterprise registration and legal publicity declaration (immatriculation) including UBO declaration
NUANS name search report (mandatory prior to name reservation or numbered company decision)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Corporations Canada / REQ-approved NUANS search agent
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market tariff for certified NUANS search

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Certified translation of foreign constitutional documents and UBO identity documents into English/French
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing per-page market rate (approximately CAD 40-60 per page)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarization, Hague Apostille, or Consular Legalization bundle (passport, incumbency certificate, POA, good-standing certificates)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Foreign notary public, Global Affairs Canada authentication services, or Canadian consular post
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for multi-document authentication; consular fees vary by post

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarized Power of Attorney executed before a Quebec notary for the incorporation agent
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Chambre des notaires du Quebec (notary of record)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Professional notarial tariff for a simple power of attorney

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered office / establishment address (virtual office) first-year service
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Licensed registered agent / virtual office service provider in Quebec
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark for Quebec virtual office with mail handling and service-of-process acceptance

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: AML/CFT UBO file assembly, PEP and sanctions screening (OFAC/UN/Canada) for all directors, officers, and UBOs
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark; 1.5-2.0 hours of senior paralegal or compliance analyst time

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Contingency reserve for supplementary apostilles, additional name refilings, or expedited translations
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Estimated contingency buffer on statutory and market tariffs

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Quebec Business Corporations Act (QBCA), CQLR c S-31.1, ss. 10-16 (incorporation), s. 30 (articles), s. 31 (certificate of incorporation), ss. 45-46 (share capital), s. 102 (registered office), s. 105 (record keeping), ss. 120-126 (directors).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) - Quebec Enterprise Registrar, Corporate Constitution and Registration Division
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation (Statuts constitutifs) - Form ARC-1 / REQ Online Constitution Service
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital. Shares may be issued without stated par value and consideration fixed by the board of directors. No escrow account or bank deposit is required for incorporation in Quebec.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION (ORGANIZING MEETING) RESOLVED: 1. Share Issuance: The subscription for 1,000 Class A common shares at CAD 0.10 per share is accepted; shares are issued fully paid to the founding shareholder and recorded in the share register. 2. Registered Office: The registered office is established at [street address], [city], Quebec, per section 102 of the Quebec Business Corporations Act. 3. Officers: [Name] is appointed President, [Name] Secretary, and [Name] Treasurer, each to serve until death, resignation, or removal. 4. Authorizations: The President and Secretary, acting jointly, are authorized to complete Registraire des entreprises du Québec filings and open the corporate bank account.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Name Search and Name Pre-registration (NUANS)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) - Online Name Pre-registration Service / NUANS System
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the proposed corporate name (distinctive element plus legal designation suffix, e.g., Inc., Corp., or Ltée) through the REQ online name pre-registration service. Obtain a NUANS (Newly Upgraded Automated Name Search) report to confirm availability against existing Canadian and Quebec trademarks, trade names, and business identifiers. Reserve the name for up to 120 days. Alternatively, proceed with a numbered company (e.g., 1234-5678 Quebec Inc.) to expedite incorporation.
required_dossiers: NUANS name search request or online name pre-registration form
Proposed legal designation suffix (Inc., Corp., Ltée)
Primary business activity description (ISIC 4791 / NAICS 454110)
Incorporator's full legal name and municipal address
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused, add a distinctive element, file a revised name pre-registration, or incorporate under a numbered company name and later adopt a name amendment under QBCA section 35.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) - Legal Person Constitution Service
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the Articles of Incorporation (Form ARC-1 or statutory model) specifying the corporate name, the municipal address of the Quebec registered office, the maximum number of directors or a fixed number, the authorized share structure (e.g., Class A common shares with rights attended upon), restrictions on share transfers or business activities (if any), and the incorporator's declaration of conformity (attestation de conformité). Sign the attestation; notarization is not generally required for a subscription box merchandising corporation.
required_dossiers: Completed Articles of Incorporation (ARC-1)
Name pre-registration attestation from the REQ (if name reserved)
Authorized share structure declaration (classes, rights, par value)
Number of initial directors and their identification
Incorporator's signed attestation de conformité
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the REQ issues a notice of deficiency, correct and refile the articles within the stated delay (generally 30 days) and pay any short-paid duties; if rejected, amend the constitutional elements and resubmit with the assistance of a notary or the REQ corporate service desk.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing with REQ - Certificate of Incorporation and Enterprise Registration (NEQ)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) - Legal Person Constitution and Enterprise Registration Counter
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the Articles of Incorporation electronically with the REQ through its secure online portal. Pay the electronic service fee, the enterprise registration duty, and the incorporation duty in a single transaction. Upon approval, the REQ issues the Certificate of Incorporation (Certificat de constitution) and automatically registers the enterprise, assigning the nine-digit Quebec Enterprise Number (NEQ). Verify the registered office address, the initial directors' list, and the declared activities on the REQ registration extract.
required_dossiers: Articles of Incorporation filed online
Electronic payment receipt for registration and constitution duties
Municipal address of the registered office in Quebec
List of initial directors (names, addresses, birth dates)
NEQ and registration extract confirmation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If processing is delayed, monitor the file via the REQ online service and submit a written review request; if registration data is inaccurate, file a formal correction under section 55 QBCA and request a revised attestation of registration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Organizing Meeting and Adoption of First Board Resolutions
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Internal corporate action - Board of Directors (Minute Book)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Hold the organizing meeting of the initial directors, formally observing quorum requirements. Adopt the first board resolution covering acceptance of share subscriptions, issuance of founder shares, confirmation of the registered office, appointment of officers (President, Secretary, Treasurer), approval of banking resolutions, and authorization to file all required REQ documents. Record the minutes, attach written director consents, and sign the resolution.
required_dossiers: Notice of organizing meeting or signed waiver of notice
First board resolution (pro-forma)
Directors' consents to act as directors
Share subscription forms and capital contribution receipts
Minutes of the organizing meeting
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If quorum is lost, the remaining directors may adjourn; if no quorum can be formed, the incorporator or a shareholder may appoint additional directors by written resolution. Any procedural irregularity may be ratified by a subsequent shareholder or board resolution.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Establishment of Statutory Books and Corporate Records (Minute Book and Registers)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Internal corporate action - Registered Office / Corporate Secretary
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Instruct the corporate secretary to open and maintain at the corporation's registered office in Quebec the following statutory records: the register of directors (names, residential addresses, and consent dates), the share register (share issuances and transfers), the minute book containing the articles, by-laws, and resolutions, and the accounting records. Records must be retrievable at the registered office; electronic records are acceptable if they can be reproduced in tangible form within a reasonable time.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation
By-laws adopted by the board
Register of directors and director consents
Share register / stock ledger
Minute book and corporate seal (if adopted)
Registered office record (register of offices)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If records are incomplete or lost, reconstruct registers using certified REQ extracts and board resolutions; a director or shareholder may demand access to records under QBCA section 214, and any obstruction may be cured by a court order for compliance.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Federal and Provincial Tax Registrations - CRA Business Number, GST/HST, QST and Payroll
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) - Business Registration Online; Revenu Québec - Online Business Services
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the corporation with the CRA for a nine-digit Business Number (BN) and a GST/HST account if annual taxable supplies exceed CAD 30,000; voluntary GST/HST registration is recommended for cross-border subscription sales. Register with Revenu Québec for the QST account (same CAD 30,000 threshold) and for Quebec source deductions and employer contributions (QPIP, CNESST) when employees are hired. Ensure the declared activity codes match NAICS 454110 / ISIC 4791 to keep the tax risk tier at standard low risk.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation and REQ registration extract (NEQ)
Registered office municipal address
Activity description (e-commerce subscription box merchandising)
Shareholder and controlling family information (nominal register)
Corporate bank account details for refunds
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the CRA or Revenu Québec queries the registration, resubmit the REQ extract with corrected activity codes; late or missed registrations can be regularized through the voluntary disclosure program or a negotiated payment arrangement with Revenu Québec.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Municipal Business Permit, Zoning and Fire Safety Clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Municipal City Borough - Permit Office (Bureau des permis) / Local Fire Prevention Service / Régie du bâtiment du Québec (RBQ)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Confirm that the registered office and any fulfillment warehouse comply with the municipal zoning by-law applicable to retail and e-commerce warehousing. Apply for a municipal business permit or occupancy permit (certificat d'occupation) for the premises. For any commercial space accessible to employees or the public, obtain a fire safety certificate (certificat de sécurité incendie) from the local fire prevention service. If structural alterations are planned, engage an RBQ-licensed contractor and submit plans for building permit approval.
required_dossiers: Lease or proof of occupancy of the registered office and warehouse
Zoning certificate or municipal business permit application
Site plan and declared occupancy
Fire safety inspection request form
CNESST employer registration and occupational health safety attestation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the municipal permit is refused, correct the stated infractions (e.g., fire exits, occupancy classification) and reapply; appeal the decision to the municipal council or the Administrative Housing Tribunal (TAL) for zoning matters; for RBQ issues, file a corrective declaration and coordinate a verification visit.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministère de l'Environnement, de la Lutte contre les changements climatiques, de la Faune et des Parcs (MELCCFP)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Screen subscription box operations against the Quebec Environment Quality Act (LQE) and the Regulation respecting environmental impact assessment and review. A subscription box service is not a listed industrial activity, so no environmental authorization is mandatory. Implement waste management protocols under municipal bylaws, including cardboard and plastic diversion and recycling through Éco Entreprises Québec. Ensure product safety compliance with the Canada Consumer Product Safety Act for all box contents.
required_dossiers: Environmental activity screening checklist (REAFIE/PVDD)
Waste disposal and recycling service contract
Material Safety Data Sheets (MSDS) for any handled substances
Canada Consumer Product Safety Act compliance declarations for box contents
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the MELCCFP determines that an authorization is required due to an incidental activity, file the applicable declaration or request a classification review; any unknown contamination discovered on the premises must be addressed through a voluntary rehabilitation plan approved by the MELCCFP.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable - no sectoral license required for subscription box merchandising; ancillary oversight by Ministère de l'Économie, de l'Innovation et de l'Énergie (MEIE) for e-commerce investment programs
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No mandatory provincial operating license; optional municipal mercantile permit (permis d'affaires) and occupancy certificate for the fulfillment premises

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministère de l'Environnement, de la Lutte contre les changements climatiques, de la Faune et des Parcs (MELCCFP)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt - no listed activity under Section II of the Regulation respecting environmental impact assessment and review; no registration or full EIA required for warehouse-based subscription box fulfillment
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Zero industrial process discharge; commercial wastewater must meet municipal sewer by-law limits (typical BOD < 300 mg/L, TSS < 350 mg/L); VOC emissions from any confined packaging area below 250 mg/m3; packaging waste diversion per RECYC-Québec / Éco Entreprises Québec regulations; product contents compliant with the Canada Consumer Product Safety Act (S.C. 2010, c. 21)

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: CNESST employer registration and compliance with the Occupational Health and Safety Regulation (RSST); fire safety certificate (certificat de sécurité incendie) issued by the local fire prevention service; structural load inspection for warehouse racking performed by an RBQ engineer; emergency evacuation plan filed with the municipal civil protection authority under the Civil Protection Act (CQLR c S-2.2)

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) / Agence du revenu du Canada — federal GST/HST and T2 corporate income tax (portal: https://www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency); Revenu Québec — QST and Quebec Corporation Tax (portal: https://www.revenuquebec.ca/en/); Business Number registration portal: https://www.canada.ca/en/services/taxes/business-number.html
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: (1) Apply to CRA for a Business Number (BN) using Form RC1 or Business Registration Online; a non-resident corporation must provide constitutive documents, foreign corporate registration number, and a Canadian agent or contact address where no Canadian director exists. (2) Open the GST/HST account (RT) on the BN; register even if below the small-supplier threshold when carrying on business in Canada and seeking input tax credit refunds. (3) Register with Revenu Québec for QST and obtain a Québec establishment number (NEQ) using the Revenu Québec 'Register for a tax number' digital service. (4) File T2 corporate returns with CRA and Quebec corporate tax returns with Revenu Québec on a fiscal-year basis. (5) Maintain an export-documentation file (CBSA declarations, bills of lading, invoices, wire-transfer proofs) to substantiate export zero-rating.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Canada has no U.S.-style check-the-box election; legal-form classification governs (Business Corporation = entity-level taxpayer). Statutory elections available to the taxpayer include: ITA s. 216 election (net-basis taxation of Canadian-source rental income for non-residents); ITA s. 217 election (net-basis taxation of certain trust or estate payments to non-residents); ITA s. 93(1) election (deemed-disposition basis for foreign-affiliate FAPI distributions); ITA s. 87 amalgamation elections; and GST/HST annual-return election available to qualifying registrants under ETA s. 243. Hybrid mismatch rules (ITA ss. 18.2, 18.3, 18.6 and 20.2(2)) are mandatory (no election) and disallow deductions in hybrid and branch-mismatch arrangements for taxation years commencing after 31 December 2023, with transitional timing rules.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: GST (Goods and Services Tax) at 5% federal and QST (Quebec Sales Tax) at 9.975% provincial — VAT-style consumption tax on taxable supplies of goods and services in Canada/Quebec
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD $30,000 of taxable supplies (excluding zero-rated supplies) in the preceding four consecutive calendar quarters or in the current quarter; non-residents measure only taxable supplies made in Canada. Registration is mandatory regardless of threshold when the non-resident carries on business in Canada or seeks input tax credit refunds.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No mandatory real-time government clearance or digital stamping of invoices exists under GST/HST or QST. Tax is self-assessed through periodic returns; invoices must contain the prescribed ETA s. 223 information and be retained. Electronic filing is mandatory for GST/HST registrants with annual revenues over CAD $1M (CRA), and Revenu Québec requires electronic remittance for large registrants. The Pan-Canadian e-invoicing framework (PEPPOL BIS 3.0) is being adopted voluntarily for federal and provincial procurement (phased 2024-2026); there is no API-clearance or QR-code stamping requirement for ordinary B2C subscription-box exports.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Under ETA Sch. VI, Part V, s. 1, zero-rating applies to a supply of tangible personal property that the supplier exports as part of the supply and for which documentary evidence of export exists, provided the property is not released into, or acquired for consumption or use in, Canada before export. Under Sch. VI, Part V, s. 7, services are zero-rated when supplied to a non-resident who is not a GST/HST registrant and the service is for use wholly outside Canada. For the subscription-box model, the physical-box component shipped to a foreign billing or shipping address is zero-rated at 0% GST/QST, including ancillary freight supplied with the exported goods; the exporter retains full input tax credits on costs despite the 0% rate. Goods must be exported 'as soon as practicable' (CRA administrative comfort: within 60 days of delivery) and the supplier must retain export proof to claim refunds on a regular GST/HST return.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Canadian Export Declaration (B13A or Electronic Export Report via the CBSA Canadian Export Reporting System / CERS)
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill evidencing physical departure and foreign destination
Commercial Invoice with Incoterms (FOB/FCA), ultimate non-resident consignee, and HS/NAICS classification
Bank inward remittance evidence (SWIFT MT103 or foreign-currency credit advice) — Canadian equivalent of the Inward Remittance Certificate
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA may reassess a zero-rated export supply as taxable where documentary proof is absent or inadequate, requiring the exporter to remit 5% GST plus applicable QST (if the place of supply is Quebec) with compound daily interest under ETA s. 280 and penalties. Specifically: gross-negligence penalty of 25% of the net tax amount (ETA s. 285.1); civil penalty of 200% of the tax evaded (ETA s. 326); criminal prosecution with fines and imprisonment for evasion (ETA ss. 327-329); and CBSA administrative monetary penalties or goods seizure under the Customs Act. Revenu Québec applies parallel interest, penalties, and reassessments under the Tax Administration Act (CQLR c. A-6.002, ss. 71-97) and can claw back QST input tax refunds. Non-arm's length export sales with unpaid or deferred proceeds are treated as transfer-pricing adjustments under ITA s. 247 (10% penalty on the adjustment) plus imputed interest under ITA s. 80.4 if proceeds are not received within a reasonable time (CRA administrative expectation of 180 days).

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: The Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada) is the domestic central bank and issuing authority for the Canadian dollar; however, Canada operates no dedicated foreign-exchange-control authority. FX-related mandates are distributed among the Department of Finance Canada (financial-sector policy and economic sanctions), the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI, which prudentially supervises federally incorporated banks and takes no exchange-convertibility decisions), FINTRAC (which enforces the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act, PCMLTFA, including cross-border electronic funds transfer reporting), and Payments Canada (which operates the Lynx high-value payment system and the Automated Clearing Settlement System).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Canadian dollar is a fully convertible, independently floating currency. Canada imposes no current-account or capital-account convertibility restrictions: imports, exports, cross-border e-commerce settlements, royalty and licence fees, intercompany financing, equity injections, and profit repatriation may all be settled in CAD or any freely convertible currency without Bank of Canada authorisation. The practical impediments for a Quebec subscription-box corporation are tax-and-reporting compliance rather than FX control: (i) non-resident dividend withholding tax under Part XIII of the Income Tax Act (statutory 25%, typically reduced to 5%-15% under income tax treaties such as the Canada-US treaty and other G7/G20 double-taxation conventions), (ii) provincial obligations in Quebec (GST/HST and Quebec QST registration for importation of goods from abroad and for e-commerce merchant settlement), and (iii) international information returns such as Form T106 for non-arm's-length transactions with non-residents and Form T1135 for foreign property holdings above CAD 100,000. None of these constitutes exchange control.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Canada has no statutory timeline, mandatory conversion ratio, or repatriation obligation for export proceeds. A Canadian subscription-box exporter may retain export and cross-border merchant settlement receipts in CAD, USD, EUR, or any other currency, hold them in foreign-currency bank accounts abroad, and convert them to CAD at market rates at a time of its choosing. The only legal touchpoints applicable to the treasury are FINTRAC Large Cash Transaction Reports and Electronic Funds Transfer Reports at the CAD 10,000 threshold, Global Affairs Canada economic-sanctions screening, and the requirement that financial statements and the Quebec tax return correctly declare foreign currency position and realised/unrealised FX gains.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.onboarding_viability_tier: Medium (cooperative-model bank; excellent for Quebec-only domestic treasury, less extensive cross-border trade desks)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium-High as an auxiliary settlement rail, Medium as a primary liquidity rail. The European Union/United Kingdom Electronic Money Institution (EMI) licence has no statutory equivalent in the Canadian Banking Act; offshore digital banks and fintech rails (e.g., Wise Business, Airwallex, Payoneer, Revolut Business) are legally usable by a Quebec-incorporated corporation as prepaid pass-through accounts, but they cannot obtain independent membership in Payments Canada's Lynx/ACSS systems and therefore cannot originate Canadian domestic EFT/PAD debits or receive local CAD direct-deposit settlement in the national clearing scheme. For the ISIC 4791 subscription-box model, an offshore EMI is viable for: (1) receiving credit-card settlement from Stripe Billing in multicurrency payout balances and converting at interbank-plus-margin; (2) paying international suppliers (3PL, packaging, product sourcing) by SWIFT MT103; (3) holding FX working capital outside the Canadian banking perimeter. It is not viable as a replacement for a Schedule I bank account in Quebec for payroll, QST/GST remittance, collection of pre-authorized debits from domestic subscribers, or merchant settlement of Visa/Mastercard transactions through Canadian acquirers. The treasury blueprint therefore mandates one lead bank account at a Schedule I bank or Desjardins caisse for domestic rails, with the EMI layered as a secondary FX and international-payments tool.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Under FINTRAC's client identification rules a private corporation may be identified by an in-person presentation of primary documents or by a two-source combined-method verification; Canadian Schedule I banks, however, uniformly impose additional risk-based KYC. In current Quebec onboarding practice: (i) a resident director or the authorised signing officer must attend at least one in-branch or video-verified interview; (ii) two government-issued photo IDs (passport, driver's licence) and a Canadian or international proof-of-address are required for each individual; (iii) a certified true copy of the company's articles of incorporation and the Registraire des entreprises du Quebec (REQ) enterprise registration must be provided; (iv) non-resident directors cannot generally complete fully remote onboarding - they must appear in person at a Canadian branch, use the bank's global coverage office for identity verification, or provide a notarised and apostilled identity package. For the target low-risk profile (no statutory licence required, standard AML tier) remote/video opening is operationally feasible at RBC, TD, and BMO for a single-director Canadian-resident company; National Bank and CIBC generally still request a physical in-branch visit for corporate signatories within their Quebec and Ontario head-office networks respectively.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial-ownership opacity: no Register of Individuals with Significant Control maintained under section 21.1 of the Canada Business Corporations Act and no beneficial-ownership declaration filed with the Registraire des entreprises du Quebec (REQ).
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified REQ enterprise registration (extra-provincial declaration or Quebec registration depending on the incorporating statute), articles of incorporation with all amendments, a signed and dated register of individuals with significant control identifying every natural person holding 10% or more of shares or 25% of votes, a directors' resolution authorising account opening and appointing signatories, and a notarised attestation of the UBO waterfall down to the ultimate beneficial owners.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident directors or UBOs, particularly those with no measurable Canadian nexus or who are related to a Politically Exposed Person (PEP).
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Valid passports plus secondary photo-bearing IDs, 90-day residential proof (utility bill or bank statement) for each signatory, a tax-residence certificate issued by the relevant revenue authority or W-8BEN-E where applicable, a signed PEP self-declaration (FINTRAC-compliant), and a source-of-funds narrative supported by personal bank statements evidencing the capital pathway for the opening deposit.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: E-commerce processing profile: subscription-box merchant settlement flowing through Stripe Billing and Authorize.Net creates high-frequency, ticket-size-variable credit patterns that can be mistaken for money-service-business (MSB) activity or third-party aggregation.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: The signed merchant acquiring agreement with Stripe and Authorize.Net demonstrating settlement in the corporate name, a chargeback and refund policy with a documented chargeback rate under 1%, evidence of physical-goods dispatch (courier manifests, customs-entry reports), and a written analysis confirming that the corporation sells its own goods and thus falls outside the PCMLTFA money-services business registration requirement.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Address or nexus inconsistency: virtual registered-office addresses, mail-drop administrative addresses, or a stated principal place of business that does not correspond to the operational logistics footprint of a physical subscription-box business.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed lease or sub-lease for the Quebec warehouse/office, a utility invoice in the corporate name, updated REQ principal-business-address filing, the GST/HST and QST registration confirmation letters, operational logistics contracts (3PL, courier) in the corporate name, and recent CRA tax documents (notice of assessment, business number).

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions- and jurisdiction-related screening flags: overseas supplier locations, non-arm's-length intercompany wires, or receipts from foreign subscribers who pay via high-risk instruments or jurisdictions.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A negative-news and sanctions-screen explanation letter, a list of all beneficial-owner nationalities and residencies, supplier due-diligence questionnaires and counterparty sanctions attestations, the import/export customs documentation (bill of lading, customs broker instructions), and a written confirmation that subscription payments do not involve virtual currency, crowdfunding, or unregulated gambling-derived proceeds.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Recommended inbound rails. (1) Equity and shareholder-loan injections are executed by SWIFT MT103 single customer credit transfers to the designated CAD operating account. If both the remitting and beneficiary banks are Payments Canada Lynx participants, the credit is final and irrevocable in central-bank money on the same business day; sub-CAD 100,000 flows settle normally on T+1 through the Automated Clearing Settlement System (ACSS). (2) Merchant settlement from Stripe Billing and Authorize.Net is routed through their Canadian acquiring entities as ACSS credit-file settlements to the corporate settlement account, reflecting a one-day funding delay and a standard merchant-clear charge. (3) Purpose coding: Canada imposes no forced FX-purpose-code regime, but the treasury must instruct each incoming wire to carry an accurate remittance narrative in the SWIFT Remittance Information field (e.g., Equity Injection, Shareholder Loan - Working Capital, Subscription Revenue - Cross-Border E-Commerce, Supplier Refund); banks use this narrative to underpin FINTRAC electronic-funds-transfer reporting at the CAD 10,000 level and to characterise the flow for CRA Form T106 and income-tax-treaty purposes. (4) File verification: the account-opening compliance file must pre-contain the share subscription agreement, board minutes authorising capital raising, a certified share-register extract, and bank reference statements for any non-bank originator. There is no central-bank approval or exchange-control permit step in Canada.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: The clearing-rail matrix for outbound settlements is: (i) SWIFT MT103 (or MT103 COV where third-party correspondents are interposed) for direct payment to foreign suppliers of subscription-box goods, providing full remittance instructions, end-to-end tracking, and same-day value where both sides are connected to the Society for Worldwide Interbank Financial Telecommunication (SWIFT); (ii) commercial documentary Letters of Credit under UCP 600, with document examination under ISBP 745 and, where the beneficiary requires a bank undertaking in the seller's country, a confirmed credit as the structured instrument for high-value ocean-freight or air-cargo inventory purchases from Asia; (iii) USD-denominated disbursements executed without double conversion by drawing on a USD operating account and clearing through Fedwire or CHIPS via the Canadian bank's US-dollar endpoint; (iv) domestic CAD disbursements to Quebec/Ontario warehouses, couriers, and 3PLs via ACSS EFT credits, or by a same-day Lynx payment for urgent or high-value outlays; and (v) recurring treasury obligations (hosting, SaaS licences, customs-broker fees) implemented by pre-authorized debits under the applicable Payments Canada rulebook. The bank's treasury desk should output ISO 20022 or SWIFT FIN MT formatted statements and FX translation advice so that the Quebec corporate treasury can reconcile outbound disbursements against the QST/GST input-credit base.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Spot FX transactions (deliverable, valued at T+2 for CAD-USD and T+1 for CAD-GBP/CAD-EUR) for immediate conversion of cross-border subscription receipts

Outright FX forwards (deliverable plain-vanilla OTC contracts, standard tenors from 1 month to 2 years, documented under an ISDA 2002 Master Agreement) to lock inventory-import costs and profit-repatriation rates
FX swaps (principal conversion plus re-exchange on a future date) used for intercompany liquidity windows without creating a continuous open position
Cross-currency interest-rate swaps (XCCY or CCS) for term-matching if the treasury draws foreign-currency debt against CAD subscription cash flow

European-style vanilla FX options and option combinations (collars, zero-cost structures, straddles) to protect subscription-box margin against adverse CAD-USD and CAD-EUR moves while retaining upside participation

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) on CAD (permissible in principle but generally non-quoted in the wholesale market because CAD is freely deliverable; included only for counterparties that structurally cannot settle CAD)
Negative-basis-hedging structures embedded in dual-currency bank accounts and sweep facilities that offset USD receipts against USD supplier liabilities without a separate derivative instrument

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Declaration (déclaration annuelle) — Registraire des entreprises du Québec
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (Government of Quebec, legal publicity register)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after the anniversary of the enterprise's registration in the Quebec enterprise register; filed annually each year thereafter.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing tariffs and administrative penalties under the Quebec Enterprise Legal Publicity Act (CQLR c P-44.1); persistent non-filing may lead to radiation/strike-off from the enterprise register, terminating juridical personality and exposing directors to continuing liability for corporate obligations.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Federal Annual Return (CBCA) — applicable if entity is incorporated under the Canada Business Corporations Act
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Corporations Canada, Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada (ISED)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after each anniversary of the corporation's incorporation or continuance.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file for two consecutive years is a statutory ground for administrative dissolution by the Director; late or non-filing may also attract offence penalties and director liability for company debts after dissolution.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory audit is not imposed by revenue, asset, or employee thresholds for a private federal/Quebec business corporation; audit is compulsory for reporting/distributing corporations and in any year shareholders do not unanimously waive the auditor's appointment. Private corporations may waive audit by unanimous shareholder consent or resolution for that fiscal year.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Canadian GAAP: IFRS for public/reporting issuers; Canadian ASPE (Part II of the CPA Canada Handbook) is available for private enterprises, including subscription-box retailers; financial statements must be placed before shareholders within 6 months after fiscal year-end where required by corporate law and tax filings.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: No separate annual UBO filing exists; significant-control details are confirmed through the Quebec annual declaration and, where applicable, the CBCA annual return. A share transfer that creates or ceases significant control must be reflected in the Register of Individuals with Significant Control within 15 days; the register must be current before filing the annual declaration/annual return.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Individuals with Significant Control
Minute Book containing director and shareholder resolutions and minutes
Share transfer register and corporate records required by CBCA/QBCA

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 3,500–8,500 per audit for a low-risk private subscription-box corporation

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 26.5% combined headline rate (federal 15% after 10% provincial abatement and 13% general rate reduction; Quebec provincial 11.5%).
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: CCPC Small Business Deduction: combined effective rate of 12.2% (federal 9% + Quebec 3.2%) on the first C$500,000 of qualifying active business income; SR&ED refundable investment tax credit of 33.3% for qualifying CCPC expenditures; Quebec Investment and Innovation Credit (C3i) for R&D; accelerated capital cost allowance for qualifying clean energy equipment; no standalone statutory tax holiday applies to subscription box retailing.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Federal: T2 Corporation Income Tax Return filed with the Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) via approved E-file software, CRA My Business Account, or designated tax preparation service providers.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual for each taxation year; quarterly installments of Part I tax payable required where the corporation's federal tax payable exceeds C$3,000.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: On or before six months after the corporation's taxation year-end (e.g., a December 31 year-end return is due June 30 of the following year); no statutory extension is available for the T2 return.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal corporate name, registered office address, and mailing address.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the exact name registered under the Canada Business Corporations Act or Quebec Business Corporations Act; provide a Canadian registered office and service address; non-resident shareholding particulars are not required in this box.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Business Number (BN) and program account identifier (CRA RP account).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A Quebec corporation must hold a CRA BN for corporate income tax, GST/HST, and payroll remittances; the RP account is used for all T2 filings and installment payments.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxation year-end date in YYYYMMDD format.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Align the taxation year with the parent's fiscal calendar only where commercially justified; otherwise CRA may challenge the period under GAAR and transfer pricing rules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income, federal rate (38%), provincial abatement (10%), general rate reduction (13%), and Part I tax otherwise payable.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The Quebec-resident corporation computes Part I tax on worldwide income; foreign-source income must be reported but may be relieved by the foreign tax credit; no reduced rate is automatic for non-resident-owned corporations unless treaty-allocated.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: SBD claimed on active business income up to the C$500,000 business limit.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: SBD eligibility requires CCPC status and a Quebec permanent establishment; a US parent may own all shares, but the corporation must carry on an active business with Quebec employees and premises; passive investment income and specified corporate income reduce the limit.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Transfer pricing disclosure for reportable transactions with non-resident related parties.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report all transactions with the US parent (management fees, royalty, inventory purchases, loans) above C$1,000,000; provide simultaneous documentation under subsection 247(4) prior to filing.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late T2 filing penalty of 5% of unpaid tax, plus 1% per full month of delay up to 12 months; repeated failure penalty of 10% plus 2% per month up to 20 months; gross negligence penalty of 50% of the understated tax; daily compound interest at the CRA prescribed rate; Revenu Québec imposes a parallel penalty structure on the CO-17.
